title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-prem Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments covering VPC and on-prem reference architectures, on-prem packaging guidance, day-2 operational procedures, and detailed upgrade/rollback playbooks. It is intended for platform engineers, site-reliability engineers, and customer success teams supporting Private (VPC & on-prem) installations.

Scope:
- Reference network and compute architectures for common customer topologies (single-rack on-prem, multi-AZ VPC, hybrid).
- Minimum and recommended hardware/software packaging for on-prem installers.
- Day-2 operations: monitoring, backups, capacity scaling, security patching.
- Deterministic upgrade and rollback procedures with pre/post checks and automated safety gates.
- Customer requirements checklist used during pre-sales and onboarding.

1) Intro and goals
- Goal: provide repeatable, secure, and observable deployments that meet Redwood SLA targets (p99 latency targets per model profile and 99.9% availability for control plane components).
- Audience: eng-private-deployments, eng-sre, solutions engineering, customer devops.

2) Reference architectures (high level)
- Single-rack on-prem (recommended for PoC and small clusters)
  - Components: 3 control-plane nodes (HA), 3+ GPU worker nodes, shared NFS/SMB for artifacts, local KMS/HSM optional.
  - Networking: private management network, VLANs for control plane and GPU traffic, out-of-band console access.
  - Typical capacities: 4x A100 40GB GPUs supports ~120 concurrent small prompt workers depending on batching.

- Multi-rack / data-center on-prem (production)
  - Components: dedicated management cluster, separate GPU cluster per workload type, multi-rack leaf/spine L3 design, redundancy across UPS and PDU.
  - Storage: distributed object store (S3-compatible) with replication, high-IO local NVMe for model cache.

- VPC deployment (cloud private)
  - Components: Private control plane in customer VPC with either customer-managed or Redwood-managed control endpoints, dedicated GPU subnets, NAT gateways for outbound updates, VPC endpoints for S3 and other services.
  - Regions & AZs: deploy control plane across 2 AZs for HA, GPU pools can be regional with placement groups for latency.

Architectural considerations / diagrams (textual):
- Diagram A: Single-rack on-prem
  - [Mgmt VLAN] -> {control-plane nodes (k8s control-plane)}
  - [GPU VLAN] -> {gpu-node-01..N} -> local NVMe -> model-cache
  - Optional: HSM connected via PCIe or network for KMS.

- Diagram B: VPC (multi-AZ)
  - AZ-1: control-plane-1,gpu-pool-1,elb-private
  - AZ-2: control-plane-2,worker-2,elb-private
  - Cross-AZ replication for object store and Redis state.

3) On-prem packaging and installer options
- Packaging formats supported:
  - Terraform + Helm charts (recommended for cloud/VPC deployments).
  - Ansible + container images for air-gapped on-prem installs.
  - OCI tarball with preloaded images + installer binary for fully air-gapped customers.

- Minimum software versions (table):
| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Kubernetes | 1.26 | 1.27 | Control-plane components verified on 1.27. |
| Helm | 3.8 | 3.10 | |
| Containerd | 1.6 | 1.7 | We validate containerd for GPU passthrough. |
| Nvidia drivers | 525.xx | 535.xx | Match driver to CUDA for chosen runtime. |
| CUDA | 11.8 | 12.1 | Required for optimized kernels. |

- Hardware and packaging (table):
| Role | Min CPU | Min RAM | NVMe | GPU | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Control-plane node | 8 vCPU | 32 GB | 200 GB | none | HA pair/trio recommended |
| GPU worker | 32 vCPU | 256 GB | 2 TB NVMe | 1x A100 or 4x T4 | Local NVMe used for model cache, swap disabled |
| Storage node | 16 vCPU | 128 GB | 10 TB HDD+NVMe cache | none | Run S3-compatible object store |

Packaging steps (air-gapped):
1. Collect inventory file (hosts.yaml) with node roles, IPs, MACs, and rack IDs.
2. Prepare OCI tarball: registry images, helm charts, and signed artifacts.
3. Transfer tarball to bastion node and load images: ctr -a /run/containerd/containerd.sock images import bundle.tar.gz
4. Run installer: ./redwood-install.sh --inventory hosts.yaml --mode airgap --kms-endpoint file://local-kms

Example installer flags:
- ./redwood-install.sh --inventory hosts.yaml --namespace redwood --helm-values values-prod.yaml --dry-run

4) Network & security requirements
- Ports (required):
  - 6443 TCP (k8s API) - control-plane
  - 2379-2380 TCP (etcd) - control-plane nodes only
  - 6379 TCP (Redis) internal cluster
  - 443/80 TCP (control-plane ingress) - optional for management endpoints
  - 22 TCP (bastion) - management only, limited to customer IP allowlist

- Firewall rules: deny-all by default between VLANs, allow explicit port flows for control-to-worker and worker-to-storage.
- TLS: all inter-service traffic must use mTLS; certs issued by customer PKI or Redwood CA.
- Key management: integrate with customer KMS where possible; if unavailable, use HSM appliance or local sealed secret with operational procedures for key rotation.

5) Day-2 operations (runbook highlights)
- Monitoring & observability
  - Metrics: export GPU utilization (nvidia-smi exporter), model cache hit rates, request latency per model, and queue depth.
  - Alerts (examples):
    - GPU memory saturation > 90% for 5m -> paging action and scale event.
    - Model cache hit rate < 50% for 10m -> investigate eviction policy.
    - Control-plane API error rate > 1% over 10m -> alert eng-sre oncall.
  - Dashboards: prebuilt Grafana dashboard templates included in charts (control-plane, gpu-pools, requests).

- Backups & recovery
  - Etcd snapshot cadence: daily snapshot retained 30 days, replicate to offsite object store.
  - Redis persistence: AOF enabled with daily exports.
  - Model artifacts: immutable model bundles stored in S3-compatible store with versioning.

- Scaling and capacity management
  - Horizontal: add GPU workers using the installer with new host entries then run helm upgrade to add node pools.
  - Vertical: replace GPU node with larger flavor following upgrade procedure (drain, cordon, swap hardware).
  - Autoscaling: customer can enable batch autoscaling policy for workload types - configure thresholds in values.yaml.

6) Upgrade procedure (major releases) - recommended steps
Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Verify health: all k8s pods Ready, control-plane SLOs met for 72h.
- Snapshot etcd: etcdctl snapshot save /backups/etcd-preupgrade-<ts>.db
- Export configs: helm get values redwood > values-before-<ts>.yaml
- Ensure available capacity: at least 1 spare GPU node for canary testing.

Canary upgrade (recommended):
1. Create canary GPU pool: add 1-2 nodes labeled canary.
2. Deploy new runtime/images to canary pool: helm upgrade --set nodeSelector.pool=canary redwood ./charts/redwood --wait --timeout 10m
3. Run smoke tests against canary: run e2e smoke suite (tests/smoke/run_smoke.py --endpoint <canary>).
4. Verify metrics: latency within 5% of baseline, error rate <0.1% for 1h.
5. If pass, progressively rollout to remaining pools (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30m observation windows.

Rollback procedure (if canary or partial rollout fails):
1. Immediately halt the rollout (helm rollback or set image to previous tag for the canary label).
2. Repoint traffic away from failing nodes: update routing policy to fallback pool.
3. Restore any modified configs from values-before-<ts>.yaml.
4. If cluster state is corrupted, restore etcd snapshot: etcdctl snapshot restore /backups/etcd-preupgrade-<ts>.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restored && restart control-plane nodes from restored data.

Emergency rollback (last resort):
- If the control-plane is degraded and quick rollback is required, follow the emergency restore runbook in the runbooks folder: runbook: emergency-control-plane-restore. Steps include isolating clusters, mounting preupgrade etcd, and validating leader election.

7) Checklist: customer requirements library (pre-onboarding)
- Networking:
  - Private network with VLAN separation and management bastion.
  - Outbound HTTPS (443) to Redwood update endpoints if customer allows automatic updates.
- Hardware:
  - Confirm GPU type, driver support, and rack power per node.
  - Rack space and cooling verification for GPU density.
- Security & compliance:
  - KMS integration plan or HSM appliance details.
  - Audit logging policy and log retention requirements.
- Operations:
  - Oncall escalation contacts and runbook handover schedule.
  - Backup targets and retention windows.

8) Operational ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (oncall rotation: private-deployments@redwood.example.com).
- SRE escalation: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.example.com.
- Customer success onboarding: customer-success@redwood.example.com.

9) Appendix: useful CLI snippets and examples
- Load images (airgapped):
  - ctr -n k8s.io images import /tmp/redwood-images.tar.gz
- Drain and cordon nodes safely:
  - kubectl cordon gpu-node-123
  - kubectl drain gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Etcd snapshot example:
  - ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 snapshot save /backups/etcd-20260420.db --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/etcd/peer.key

10) Links & references
- Internal runbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-deployment-runbook-2028-03-01
